title: Negative stamp values extend postage range, and mutual information subadditivity fails
summary: This week settled several open problems across discrete mathematics and information theory. It was established that allowing negative denominations strictly increases the consecutive integers reachable by postage stamp combinations. In information theory, subadditivity of mutual information was refuted for Hellinger distance and quarter-power divergences. In graph theory, new findings classified when spectral bounds on clique numbers hold, answered questions about permutation groups generated by graph hops, and established exact covering numbers for powers of cycle graphs.

lead.title: Negative stamp values expand the consecutive postage amounts 8 stamps can reach
lead.story:
Imagine a postal system where every parcel must carry an exact total value using at most 8 stamps from a fixed menu of 4 denominations, one of which can be 0. Mathematicians study how far an unbroken run of consecutive integer postage amounts can stretch before encountering a value that cannot be paid.

When all stamp denominations must be positive, an exhaustive search established that the longest possible consecutive run with 4 denominations covers every integer from 0 up to 89, achieved by denominations of 0, 1, 9, and 14. It was long believed that allowing negative denominations—effectively giving the recipient the ability to return change—could not increase this threshold in such small systems.

That expectation fails for 8 stamps. A newly verified construction shows that choosing the 4 denominations -4, 1, 13, and 14 forms an unbroken chain of valid sums reaching all the way to 99.

Allowing a single negative denomination provides extra flexibility that surpasses every purely positive collection of the same size, proving that negative entries strictly increase the span of 4-stamp sets.

fields.name: Elementary Number Theory
fields.context: Verified that negative denominations strictly improve 4-denomination postage stamp ranges at order 8, and checked lower bounds for zero-sum Davenport constants in planar integer boxes.

results.headline: Four stamps with one negative value reach 99 consecutive postage amounts
results.plain: Allowing one negative value among 4 stamp types lets 8 stamps reach more consecutive totals than any 4 positive stamp types.
results.before: With 4 non-negative stamp denominations and at most 8 stamps, the maximum unbroken range of postage amounts starting from 0 was known to be 89.
results.answer: The set {-4, 1, 13, 14} forms an 8-basis for 99, proving that allowing a negative denomination strictly increases the maximal postage range from 89 to at least 99.
results.why: Disproves the intuition that positive denominations are always optimal for small stamp collections, demonstrating the advantage of negative values.
results.idea: Evaluates the reachable integers of {-4, 1, 13, 14} and shows every integer from 0 to 99 is an 8-fold sum of its elements.

results.headline: Davenport constant of two-dimensional integer boxes bounded via minimal zero sums
results.plain: Long sequences in two-dimensional integer grids can avoid having sub-sequences that sum to zero up to a precise length.
results.before: The maximal length of zero-sum-free sequences in planar integer boxes was conjectured to be governed by the smallest prime not dividing the box radius.
results.answer: arXiv:2610.16562 shows the Davenport constant of the box ⟦-m, m⟧² is at least 4m² - q(m), where q(m) is the smallest prime not dividing m; Lean now checks the proof.
results.why: Establishes the exact lower bound for zero-sum sequences in planar boxes by verifying minimality of the extremal sequence.
results.idea: Constructs an explicit zero-sum sequence on 3 vectors and proves that no non-empty proper sub-sequence sums to zero.

fields.name: Combinatorics for TCS
fields.context: Settled the equivalence covering number of cycle cubes for lengths congruent to 2 modulo 4, and formalized bounded-defect Mondrian partitions.

results.headline: Equivalence covering number of cycle cubes equals 4 when length is 2 modulo 4
results.plain: Covering all edges of a third-power cycle graph with equivalence relations requires 4 relations whenever the cycle length leaves remainder 2 upon division by 4.
results.before: For cycle cubes of even length not divisible by 4, previous work left the equivalence covering number open between 3 and 4.
results.answer: For every n ≥ 10 with n ≡ 2 (mod 4), the equivalence covering number of the cube of the n-cycle is exactly 4.
results.why: Settles the first open family of the cycle-power covering problem, showing the lower bound of 4 is tight.
results.idea: Proves that any 3-cover forces a rigid periodic chord structure whose cycle count requires 4 to divide the vertex number.

results.headline: Seven-rectangle Mondrian partitions achieve defect 280 infinitely often
results.plain: Tiling large squares with 7 unequal integer rectangles can keep the area difference between the largest and smallest tiles down to 280.
results.before: It was unknown whether square Mondrian dissections using 7 pairwise non-congruent rectangles could achieve uniformly bounded area defects for arbitrarily large squares.
results.answer: arXiv:2610.19193 proves infinitely many squares admit 7-rectangle non-congruent dissections with defect 280, giving liminf defect at most 280; Lean now checks the proof.
results.why: Solves the bounded-defect question for 7-rectangle partitions by exhibiting an infinite family of square side lengths.
results.idea: Parameterizes 7 non-congruent rectangles in a square of side 105q and relates their area defect to solutions of a Pell-type equation.

fields.name: Graph Theory & Graph Algorithms
fields.context: Classified spectral clique bounds for five-block graphs, refuted conjectures on leap groups of kayak paddle graphs, and proved dijoin symmetry for acyclic tournaments.

results.headline: Complete classification of strong spectral clique bounds for five-block graphs
results.plain: A strong formula bounding the size of the largest fully connected subgraph from matrix eigenvalues holds for five-block graphs except on three infinite families.
results.before: The strong spectral bound on clique numbers was proven for three-block and four-block graphs with isolated exceptions, but remained open for 5 blocks.
results.answer: For five-block graphs B_5, the strong spectral clique bound holds if and only if the first four block sizes do not form (1,1,1,1), (1,1,1,2), or (1,2,1,1).
results.why: Completely characterizes the domain of validity for the strengthened spectral clique bound on five-block graphs.
results.idea: Computes the quotient matrix trace of squares in closed form and evaluates the algebraic gap against the clique bound.

results.headline: Kayak paddle graphs with an even cycle never generate symmetric or alternating leap groups
results.plain: When a graph formed by 2 loops connected by a path has an even loop, its step-permutations cannot generate the full permutation group.
results.before: It was questioned whether all kayak paddle graphs admitting hops generate either the full symmetric group or the alternating group on their vertices.
results.answer: Every kayak paddle graph with an even cycle has leap group strictly smaller than the symmetric and alternating groups; the instance with cycle lengths 3 and 4 and path length 1 provides a 7-vertex counterexample.
results.why: Refutes the expectation that derangements of connected kayak paddle graphs generally generate the symmetric or alternating group.
results.idea: Shows that any hop must map the vertex set of an even cycle to itself, trapping the generated group inside a proper set stabilizer.

results.headline: Inversion values for tournament dijoins are symmetric when one side is transitive
results.plain: Joining 2 tournaments with all edges directed from one to the other requires the same number of reversals to become acyclic regardless of joining order if one is transitive.
results.before: Conjecture 4.1 of arXiv:2610.13798 posited that the inversion count of a dijoin of 2 tournaments is invariant under swapping the 2 components.
results.answer: The symmetry inv(D₁ → D₂) = inv(D₂ → D₁) holds whenever D₁ is acyclic, with both sides equal to the inversion count of D₂.
results.why: Confirms the symmetry conjecture for tournament dijoins in the broad case where at least one component has no directed cycles.
results.idea: Squeezes the dijoin inversion count between the maximum and the sum of component inversion counts, which coincide when one is acyclic.

fields.name: Information Theory & Coding
fields.context: Refuted subadditivity of mutual f-information for power divergences, constructing explicit counterexamples for the Hellinger divergence and quarter-power divergences.

results.headline: Mutual information subadditivity fails for Hellinger divergence and quarter-power divergences
results.plain: Information about a source shared across 2 conditionally independent observations can strictly exceed the sum of the individual shared informations.
results.before: It was conjectured that mutual f-information generated by power divergences satisfies subadditivity under Markov chains Y ← X → Z for all β between 0 and 1.
results.answer: Subadditivity fails for Hellinger mutual information at β = 1/2 on binary variables, and for the power divergence at β = 1/4 on ternary variables.
results.why: Disproves subadditivity for power divergences in the lower parameter range, restricting potential subadditivity to parameters above two-thirds.
results.idea: Constructs explicit discrete channels where joint mutual information strictly exceeds the sum of marginal mutual informations.

fields.name: Foundations of Cryptography
fields.context: Extended witness extraction for Schnorr protocols to affine-related public keys that share commitments, establishing explicit algebraic soundness bounds.

results.headline: Schnorr identification extracts witnesses from transcripts sharing commitments under affine-related keys
results.plain: Secret keys can be mathematically recovered if 2 digital proof transcripts reuse the same initial commitment across related keys.
results.before: Schnorr witness extraction traditionally assumes 2 transcripts generated with the same public key and distinct challenges.
results.answer: A secret witness w₁ is efficiently extracted from 2 Schnorr transcripts with identical commitments under affine-related keys w₂ = α·w₁ + β whenever s₁ - α⁻¹·s₂ - α⁻¹·β·c₂ is invertible modulo q.
results.why: Proves soundness of Schnorr proofs under affine related-key attacks, showing shared commitments compromise security across distinct related keys.
results.idea: Cross-multiplies verification equations to cancel the shared commitment and solves the resulting linear exponent equation modulo q.

fields.name: Online Algorithms
fields.context: Formalized the lower bound of k + 1/2 on the competitive ratio of deterministic deadline paging, confirming that deadlines strictly increase paging difficulty.

results.headline: Deterministic deadline paging competitive ratio is bounded below by k plus a half
results.plain: Algorithms managing memory caches with deadlines cannot be better than k plus a half times the offline optimum.
results.before: Competitive ratios for deterministic online paging with deadlines were known to exceed the classical bound k of standard paging.
results.answer: arXiv:2610.18767 proves that for cache size k and at least k + 2 pages, no deterministic online algorithm achieves competitive ratio strictly less than k + 1/2; Lean now checks the proof.
results.why: Establishes that the presence of deadlines strictly worsens the optimal competitive ratio of online paging from k to at least k + 1/2.
results.idea: Constructs an adversarial request sequence with deadlines that forces excessive cache misses on any online strategy.

fields.name: Fair Division
fields.context: Formalized separation results showing that randomized mechanisms with subsidies can satisfy fairness simultaneously in expectation and ex post, even where pure allocations cannot.

results.headline: Best-of-both-worlds fair lotteries exist even when deterministic fair allocations do not
results.plain: A lottery over item distributions can guarantee fairness both on average and in the worst case, even when no single item assignment achieves this.
results.before: It was unknown whether randomized allocations could achieve best-of-both-worlds fairness when no single deterministic allocation is simultaneously EF1 and envy-freeable with subsidies.
results.answer: arXiv:2610.14994 proves that for 3 submodular agents and 4 items, no pure allocation is both EF1 and envy-freeable, yet a randomized lottery is; Lean now checks the proof.
results.why: Demonstrates the strict superiority of randomized mechanisms with subsidies over deterministic fair division under submodular valuations.
results.idea: Verifies a concrete profile of 3 submodular agents over 4 items where every pure allocation fails one requirement while a mixture satisfies both.

outlook: Does the inversion count of a tournament dijoin satisfy symmetry for all pairs of finite tournaments?
Does the stacking pebbling number of every finite tree equal its explicit tree estimate?
Does Tuza's conjecture that the minimum triangle cover is at most twice the maximum packing hold for all finite graphs?
Is mutual f-information for power divergences subadditive under Markov chains for all parameter values from two-thirds to one?
Does the equivalence covering number of cycle powers equal m plus 2 for all even cycle lengths not divisible by 2^m?

glossary.meaning: Envy-free up to one item: any envy disappears once some single item is removed (a good from the envied bundle, or a chore from the envious agent's own).
TCS: the mathematical study of discrete algorithms, complexity, and combinatorics.

zh.title: 负面额邮票扩大邮资范围，互信息次可加性不成立
zh.summary: 本周解决了离散数学与信息论领域的数个未决问题。研究证实，允许负面额能严格增加邮票组合所能覆盖的连续整数范围。在信息论中，互信息的次可加性在赫林格距离与四分之一次方散度下被否定。在图论方面，新成果分类了团数谱界的成立条件，解答了由图跳跃生成的置换群的相关问题，并确定了圈图各次幂的精确覆盖数。

lead.title: 负面额邮票扩大8枚邮票所能覆盖的连续邮资范围
lead.story:
设想这样一个邮政系统：每个包裹必须从固定的4种面额（其中一种可以为0）中最多选用8枚邮票，贴出准确的总面值。数学家研究的是，在遇到第一个无法支付的金额之前，连续整数邮资能够不间断地延伸多远。

当所有邮票面额都必须为正时，穷举搜索表明，4种面额所能达到的最长连续区间涵盖了从0到89的每个整数，由面额0、1、9和14实现。长期以来人们认为，允许负面额——实际上相当于让收件人能够找零——在如此小规模的系统中无法提高这一上限。

这一预期在8枚邮票的情况下落空了。一项最新验证的构造表明，选取-4、1、13和14这4种面额，可以形成一条一路延伸至99的连续有效金额链。

允许单个负面额所带来的额外灵活性，超越了同等大小的任何纯正数面额集合，证明了负面额能够严格增大4面额集合的覆盖跨度。

results.headline: 含一个负面额的4种邮票可达到99个连续邮资额
results.plain: 在4种邮票中允许一个负值，可让8枚邮票达到的连续总值多于任何4种正邮票类型。

results.headline: 通过极小零和界定二维整数盒的达文波特常数
results.plain: 二维整数网格中的长序列在达到某一精确长度之前，可以避免出现和为零的子序列。

results.headline: 当圈长模4余2时圈图三次幂的等价覆盖数等于4
results.plain: 当圈的长度除以4余2时，用等价关系覆盖圈图三次幂的所有边需要4个关系。

results.headline: 7个矩形的蒙德里安分割可无穷多次达到缺陷值280
results.plain: 用7个互不相同的整数矩形密铺大正方形，可将最大与最小图块的面积差控制在280。

results.headline: 五块图强谱团数界的完全分类
results.plain: 通过矩阵特征值界定最大完全子图规模的强公式，在五块图上除3个无限族外均成立。

results.headline: 含偶圈的皮划艇桨图绝不生成对称或交错跳跃群
results.plain: 当由一条路径连接2个圈构成的图含有偶圈时，其跳步置换无法生成全置换群。

results.headline: 当一侧可传递时竞赛图有向连接的反转值具有对称性
results.plain: 若其中一个竞赛图可传递，无论连接顺序如何，将2个竞赛图单向连接后变为无圈所需的反转次数都相同。

results.headline: 赫林格散度与四分之一次方散度的互信息次可加性不成立
results.plain: 在2个条件独立观测中共享的信源信息，可以严格大于各个单独共享的信息之和。

results.headline: 施诺尔身份识别可从仿射相关密钥下共享承诺的记录中提取见证
results.plain: 若2份数字证明记录在相关密钥间复用了相同的初始承诺，便可在数学上恢复私钥。

results.headline: 确定性带截止时间分页的竞争比下界为k加1/2
results.plain: 管理带截止时间内存缓存的算法，其性能无法优于离线最优解的k加1/2倍。

results.headline: 确定性公平分配不存在时仍存在两全其美的公平抽签
results.plain: 即使没有任何单一物品分配能够做到，物品分配的抽签也能同时保证平均和最坏情况下的公平。

outlook: 对所有有限竞赛图对而言，竞赛图有向连接的反转数是否都满足对称性？
每个有限树的堆叠卵石数是否都等于其显式树估计值？
关于最小三角形覆盖至多是最大填充的2倍的图扎猜想，是否对所有有限图都成立？
对于从2/3到1的所有参数值，幂散度的互f信息在马尔可夫链下是否都满足次可加性？
对所有不能被2^m整除的偶数圈长，圈图幂的等价覆盖数是否都等于m加2？
